citations.anchor: 401s without an Authorization header
citations.why: POSTs a well-formed `tools/list` frame with no credential and asserts a transport 401 — if the protocol layer ran before authentication the frame would answer 200 with a JSON-RPC body.

citations.anchor: 401s an unauthenticated GET, before the verb is considered
citations.why: Asserts the credential-less GET is 401, so the 405 verb answer is provably unreachable without a token.

citations.anchor: does not accept a session cookie in place of a token
citations.why: Drives the endpoint with a logged-in cookie agent and asserts 401.

citations.anchor: 401s once the token is revoked
citations.why: The revoked arm: the same secret answers 200 then 401 after deletion, with the same bare status the unknown-token test asserts.

citations.anchor: 401s once the token has expired
citations.why: The expired arm: expiry answers the identical transport 401 rather than a distinguishable JSON-RPC error.

citations.anchor: 401s a bearer value carrying internal whitespace
citations.why: Sends `Bearer <valid secret> extra` and asserts 401 — rejoining the pieces would have authenticated the real secret.

citations.anchor: 403s a workspace outside the token bucket
citations.why: A `tools/list` naming a workspace outside the token's basket is 403 before any dispatch, pinning resolve-before-dispatch and the basket check.

citations.anchor: 400s a repeated ?workspaceId= instead of ignoring it
citations.why: Two named workspaces answer 400 with 'more than one workspace' rather than a silent pick of the token's own.

citations.anchor: prefers the header over the query parameter
citations.why: Header and query name different in-basket workspaces; the resolved context is the header's, pinning the precedence clause.

citations.anchor: derives permissions from the token scope, not the minting user
citations.why: A `read`-scope record with a `createdBy` user yields can(CONTENT_READ) true and can(CONTENT_CREATE) false, and the actor is the token itself; the minting user is never looked up.

citations.anchor: refuses a write tool a read token invokes by name
citations.why: `content_create` is absent from the read token's list yet invoked by name and refused with `forbidden`, so the decision provably lives in the call path, not in the listing.

citations.anchor: shows no copilot-only tool, whatever the scope
citations.why: The list half: a full-scope token's `tools/list` is asserted to contain none of the copilot-only names.

citations.anchor: refuses a copilot-only tool invoked by name
citations.why: The call half: a full-scope token naming `admin_content_search` gets an isError result.

citations.anchor: still answers a permission refusal before it reads the arguments
citations.why: A read token calls `content_delete` with nonsense arguments and gets `forbidden`, not `validation_failed`.

citations.anchor: stamps the dispatching surface on the handler
citations.why: The context handed to `call` carries no surface (createToolContext takes none); the handler nonetheless sees surface 'mcp', so it is stamped by the registry at dispatch. The 'presentation only, never authority' half is a coding rule no harness can assert.

citations.anchor: answers an unreadable resource URI with -32002 and structured data
citations.why: The resources half on the wire: `result` is absent, the frame carries error -32002, and `error.data` holds the same flattened `{code}` payload a tool refusal carries.

citations.anchor: reports a thrown HttpException as an isError result
citations.why: The tools/call half: a thrown NotFoundException comes back as a successful result with isError true and the flattened {status, code, message}, not as a JSON-RPC error.

citations.anchor: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.7:5432
citations.why: The tools/call path: a raw driver error becomes `internal_error` and the serialized result is asserted not to contain the connection detail.

citations.anchor: relation "secrets" does not exist
citations.why: The resources/read path: a raw driver error becomes -32603 / `internal_error` with the table name asserted absent from the message.

citations.anchor: emits the same value as text and as structuredContent
citations.why: Parses the text block and asserts it equals `structuredContent`, so dropping either spelling fails.

citations.anchor: boxes a non-object result
citations.why: An array, a string and null each arrive as `{ value: … }` in structuredContent rather than being dropped.

citations.anchor: refuses a tool result over the endpoint ceiling
citations.why: Boots with mcpMaxResultBytes=200 and asserts isError, code `result_too_large`, and structuredContent absent — the size ceiling in a model-readable form.

citations.anchor: abandons a tool call that outlives the endpoint deadline
citations.why: Boots with mcpCallTimeoutMs=1 and asserts a 504 / `timeout` result — the time ceiling in a model-readable form. (The 1 MB request-body ceiling is the host's, and is not exercised on this route.)

citations.anchor: hands the handler a signal that aborts on expiry
citations.why: The handler never settles yet the caller's `callTool` returns, and the signal it was handed is asserted aborted: the wait is bounded, the work is only told.

citations.anchor: survives a handler that rejects after the deadline
citations.why: A handler that ignores the deadline and rejects afterwards leaves the caller with the timeout answer and does not become an unhandled rejection.

citations.anchor: ignores an Mcp-Session-Id from a client that thinks it has one
citations.why: A POST carrying an invented Mcp-Session-Id answers 200, so no session identifier is validated. (The per-exchange teardown on `close` is not pinned by any test.)

citations.anchor: shows a read-scoped token only the read tools
citations.why: The read token's list is asserted to lack content_create/update/publish/delete.

citations.anchor: shows a full-scoped token the write tools too
citations.why: The same deployment shows a full token those very names, so the two lists provably differ by caller.

citations.anchor: leaves the copilot a full catalogue
citations.why: With mcpEnabled=false the MCP route 404s while a copilot run is still offered the registry's tools, so the switch removed only the controller.

citations.anchor: leaves the MCP endpoint a full catalogue
citations.why: The symmetric half: with the copilot disabled, `tools/list` over MCP still carries content and shared tools.

citations.anchor: owns no migrations
citations.why: Asserts the plugin definition's `migrations` is undefined, so declaring a migrations descriptor fails the test.

citations.anchor: refuses to boot when two providers claim one name
citations.why: `onApplicationBootstrap` — the hook Nest runs inside app.init() — throws on a duplicate name; sibling tests in the same block cover the invalid name, the empty surfaces, the unknown permission and the malformed inputSchema.

citations.anchor: reports every problem at once, not just the first
citations.why: The 'every problem at once' clause: a catalogue with two distinct defects throws a message asserted to name both.

citations.anchor: lists published entries only
citations.why: A seeded draft is neither returned nor counted in `total` by a default `content_list`.

citations.anchor: refuses draft visibility to a read token
citations.why: `status: 'any'` on a read-scope token (no content:update) is refused with `forbidden`, pinning that only the write permission widens the read.
